ing: shredded, such as mozzarella or queso fresco
st: Stir [[1 tsp]] salt into [[2.5 cups]] warm water in a bowl.
Slowly add [[2 cups]] cornmeal, stirring, until no lumps remain.
Let the dough rest for [[5 minutes]], then knead briefly. It should be soft and not sticky.
Divide into 8 balls and flatten each into a disc about 3/4 inch thick.
Heat [[2 tbsp]] oil in a skillet over medium heat.
Cook the arepas for 6 minutes per side until a golden crust forms.
Heat the oven to 350°F (175°C) and bake the arepas on a tray for [[15 minutes]] to cook through. They should sound hollow when tapped.
Split each open and spread with [[4 tbsp]] butter between them.
Stuff with cheese, black beans, beef and avocado.

ing: peeled and sliced on a diagonal
st: Drain the soaked beans, put in a pot with [[6 cups]] water and simmer for [[90 minutes]] until soft. Add [[1 tsp]] salt at the end.
Place the steak in a pot with [[4 cups]] water, half the onion and half the garlic. Simmer 70 minutes until it falls apart.
Shred the beef with two forks.
Heat [[2 tbsp]] oil in a skillet and cook the remaining onion, bell pepper and garlic for 6 minutes.
Add the tomatoes, [[1 tsp]] cumin, [[1 tsp]] pepper and [[1 tsp]] salt, then the beef. Cook 15 minutes.
Heat [[2 tbsp]] oil in a pot and stir in the rice for 1 minute, then add [[3 cups]] water and [[1 tsp]] salt.
Cover and cook on low for [[18 minutes]] until the rice is tender.
Fry the plantain slices in the remaining [[0.25 cup]] oil over medium heat for 3 minutes per side until caramelized.
Plate rice, beans, shredded beef and plantains side by side.
Blend [[3 cups]] corn with [[0.25 cup]] milk, [[3 tbsp]] sugar, [[3 tbsp]] cornmeal and [[0.5 tsp]] salt until mostly smooth but slightly textured.
Let the batter rest for [[10 minutes]] to thicken.
Melt [[1 tbsp]] butter in a skillet over medium-low heat.
Pour about [[0.5 cup]] batter into the skillet and spread into a round.
Cook for 4 minutes until bubbles appear and the edges set, then flip and cook 3 minutes.
Add some cheese on one half and fold the other over it.
Cook until the cheese melts. Repeat with remaining batter.
Serve hot spread with [[3 tbsp]] butter.
Heat [[2 tbsp]] annatto oil in a pot and cook the onion, pepper and garlic 6 minutes.
Add the pork and chicken, [[2 tbsp]] tomato paste and [[1 tsp]] salt and cook until cooked through, about 25 minutes. Cool.
Stir in [[0.25 cup]] olives, [[0.25 cup]] raisins and [[2 tbsp]] capers.
Mix [[4 cups]] cornmeal, [[5 cups]] warm broth, [[0.25 cup]] annatto oil and [[1 tsp]] salt into a soft dough.
Soften banana leaves over a flame or in hot water, then wipe dry.
Spread a spoonful of dough thin in the center of a leaf. Add a heaping spoonful of filling.
Fold the leaf over to enclose, wrap in a second leaf and tie tightly with string.
Boil the parcels in a large pot of water for [[60 minutes]], weighted down so they stay submerged.
Rest 10 minutes. Unwrap and eat the filled dough.

ing: firm cheese like queso blanco, cut in sticks
st: Mix [[2 cups]] flour, [[1 tsp]] salt and [[1 tsp]] sugar.
Rub in [[3 tbsp]] cold butter, then add the egg and [[0.5 cup]] cold water. Knead into a smooth dough.
Cover and rest for [[30 minutes]].
Cut the cheese into 24 sticks about 3 inches long.
Roll the dough very thin and cut strips about 1 inch wide.
Wind a strip around each cheese stick, overlapping, pinching ends to seal completely.
Heat [[3 cups]] oil to 350°F (175°C) in a deep pot.
Fry in batches for 3 minutes until golden, then drain on paper towels.
Serve hot with a dipping sauce.
Heat [[1 tbsp]] oil in a skillet and cook the onion and garlic for 4 minutes.
Add the beef, [[0.5 tsp]] cumin and [[0.5 tsp]] salt. Cook until browned to 160°F (71°C), about 8 minutes. Cool and mix in the beans.
Mix [[2 cups]] cornmeal, [[2 cups]] warm water and [[1 tsp]] salt into a soft dough.
Rest the dough for [[10 minutes]].
Divide into 10 balls. Flatten each between plastic sheets into a 5 inch circle.
Put a spoonful of beef filling and cheese on one half, fold over and seal the edges with your fingers.
Heat [[3 cups]] oil in a pan to 350°F (175°C).
Fry 3 minutes per side until golden and puffed.
Drain on paper towels and serve hot.

ing: or beef broth for no alcohol
st: Season the roast with [[2 tsp]] salt and [[1 tsp]] pepper.
Heat [[3 tbsp]] oil in a heavy pot and add [[0.5 cup]] brown sugar. Cook 4 minutes until dark and foamy.
Add the roast and turn it in the caramel until dark brown on all sides, about 10 minutes.
Add the onions, bell pepper and garlic and cook 5 minutes.
Add [[1 cup]] red wine, [[3 tbsp]] Worcestershire and [[2 cups]] broth.
Cover and simmer very gently for [[2.5 hours]], turning the roast every 30 minutes, until very tender.
Move the roast to a board and rest for [[15 minutes]].
Simmer the sauce uncovered until thickened, about 10 minutes. Slice the beef and spoon sauce over.
Heat the oven to 350°F (175°C). Boil water for a water bath.
Cook [[0.75 cup]] sugar with [[3 tbsp]] water in a saucepan over medium heat until amber, about 8 minutes, without stirring.
Pour the caramel into a 9 inch cake pan and tilt to coat the bottom.
Blend the eggs, condensed milk, [[1.5 cups]] milk and [[1 tsp]] vanilla until smooth.
Pour the mixture over the caramel. Cover tightly with foil.
Set the pan in a roasting dish and add hot water halfway up the sides.
Bake [[60 minutes]] until set with a slight jiggle.
Cool, then chill at least [[3 hours]].
Run a knife around the edge, invert onto a plate and serve.
Scoop the avocado flesh into a blender.
Add the bell pepper, onion, garlic and cilantro.
Add [[2 tbsp]] vinegar, [[0.25 cup]] oil and [[1 tsp]] salt.
Add [[0.25 cup]] water and blend to a thick, slightly textured sauce.
Taste and add more salt or vinegar as needed.
Chill for [[30 minutes]] so the flavors blend.
Serve with grilled meat, arepas or empanadas.
